text: A glass pane, a Copper Resonator and a Spirit Shard make a lens for ley sight. Look through it and you see what the land and your camp are doing: how strong the ley is, where Pulse reaches, which totems are awake and which machines are working.

pages.title: Five sights
text: Hold it in either hand and use it to cycle through five sights:
- **Ley**: draws the ley lines around you, each thread in its voice's colour.

- **Pulse zone**: shows the lattice network you stand on: the **8-block** reach of its conductors, the one you tap outlined brightest, and a mark over every block that holds Pulse. The panel names the network's conductors and rate, your conductor's rank and what it carried last second, and totals the network's Pulse coming in against what its machines spend. Off the lattice it says so.
- **Voices**: marks nearby totems in their own voice's colour when answered, a darker shade when dim, and grey when quiet.
- **Machines**: marks the Tribal Power machines around you.
- **Off**: the glass goes dark. No lines, no panel, no marks. Ley goggles you are wearing still show their threads.

Each sight has its own panel on your screen. Ley sight shows the ley strength where you stand, Pulse zone what is stored and flowing, Voices the voices in reach, and Machines the stations, relays and caches around you. Off shows nothing.

pages.title: Ley threads
text: The ley lines are a web across the whole dimension: the planet's Pulse, not blocks. Each line is one thread in a Resonance Totem's colour (earth green, fire orange, water blue, air pale sky, spirit violet or loom gold), with a bright node pulsing along it.

A totem pulls the thread of its own colour through itself, so you can steer a thread by where you stand the totem. A crossing lies roughly every **80 blocks**. Most join two to four threads, and only about one in forty brings all six together.

Craft a Ley Lens into a [Spiritweave Hood](spiritweave) and the hood's goggles show the same threads while you wear it, even with a lens in hand set to Off; a lens held on another sight hides them. Sneak-use the hood, or sneak-click with an empty hand while it is on your head, to turn the goggles off and on.

pages.title: Reading the ground
pages.text: The lens draws only the threads, never the ground. In ley sight the strength bar on your panel turns gold where a Ley Collector would sing loudest and blue where it would barely hum.

pages.title: Up close
text: Sneak-use the lens on a Ley Collector to print that collector's exact factor breakdown in chat: the same numbers it collects with.
Sneak-use it on a March creature, wild or bonded, to print its threads and Marks; see [Bonding a familiar](familiars).

The strength line is the same beat a collector would count there, from 1 to **16**, shown as a share of the full 16. The land's share stops at 6, and each ley line adds up to 2, less the farther you stand from it. A beat of **8 or more** keeps nearby totems awake. A roof takes away sky, rain and storm, but the lines stay, so a roofed collector gets weaker, not dead.
